sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT shows calcified gallstones in the gallbladder. Gallstones may be of variable attenuation with calcified gallstones easiest to appreciate on CT or radiography.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: RP-01

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT shows prominent calcification of the gallbladder wall , compatible with a porcelain gallbladder. The association between porcelain gallbladder and gallbladder carcinoma is now considered somewhat debatable.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: RP-02

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT shows large, heterogeneously calcified mass lesions in the liver as well as a similarly calcified lymph node mass in the gastrohepatic ligament. These findings reflect metastases from the patient's primary mucinous colon cancer.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: RP-03

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT shows multiple punctate calcifications in the spleen, likely related to old, healed granulomatous disease.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: RP-04

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial NECT shows an incidentally discovered benign splenic cyst with prominent peripheral calcification. Acquired splenic cysts are more likely to demonstrate calcification compared to congenital splenic cysts.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: RP-05

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial NECT shows a large, heavily calcified mass in the liver with a characteristically whorled or serpiginous pattern of calcification. This represents a large, chronic echinococcal cyst in a patient who had emigrated from an endemic area.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: RP-06

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT in a patient status post liver transplant shows patchy areas of calcification throughout the liver parenchyma, which were found on biopsy to represent the sequelae of ischemia and rejection.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: RP-07

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial NECT shows an atrophic pancreas with extensive calcification, findings diagnostic of chronic pancreatitis.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: RP-08

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT shows a solid, enhancing mass in the pancreatic body with internal coarse calcification, representing a pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: RP-09

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT in a young woman shows a large solid and pseudopapillary neoplasm (SPEN) with a sizable central coarse calcification .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: RP-10

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial NECT shows a massive staghorn renal calculus almost completely filling the right intrarenal collecting system.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: RP-11

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Coronal NECT shows a large, right-sided renal mass with subtle internal calcifications , found to represent a chromophobe renal cell carcinoma at surgical resection.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: RP-12

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial NECT shows a large, high-density stone within the bladder.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: RP-13

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT shows a large pelvic mass in a young female patient with extensive internal fat, a discrete fat-fluid level , and internal calcification , compatible with a dermoid cyst.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: RP-14

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial NECT in a female patient shows a large, cystic pelvic mass with extensive calcification , found to represent an ovarian cancer.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: RP-15

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT shows a large, calcified mass in the pelvis, representing a primary ovarian malignancy, with additional calcified tumor implants in the peritoneum and anterior pelvic wall .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: RP-16

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial NECT shows multiple calcified injection granulomas in the subcutaneous fat of the buttocks.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: RP-17

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Coronal CECT shows a linear, ossified scar along a prior midline abdominal incision.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: RP-18

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial NECT shows extensive calcifications in the subcutaneous soft tissues and musculature of the pelvis in a patient with scleroderma.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: RP-19

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial NECT in a patient with end-stage renal disease shows shrunken, end-stage kidneys and extensive upper abdominal arterial vascular tram-track calcifications .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: RP-20

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Frontal radiograph shows multiple phleboliths in the pelvis (having their typical distribution) mainly below the iliac spines, some with central lucency .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: RP-21

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Coronal NECT shows an atretic appearance of the IVC and iliac veins, with extensive linear calcification in the inferior vena cava (IVC) and external iliac veins , findings compatible with the patient's known history of chronic deep venous thrombosis.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: RP-22

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Coronal CECT shows a large, tubular, cystic mass with subtle peripheral calcification . On close inspection, this cystic mass connected with the cecum, representing a large appendiceal mucocele.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: RP-23

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT in a patient with history of treated non-Hodgkin lymphoma shows a residual soft tissue mass with calcification in the mesentery, representing the sequelae of treatment. The mass was stable over several exams and was not metabolically active on PET.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: RP-24

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT shows extensive calcification of the peritoneal lining and along the surface of bowel loops (along with loculated ascites) in a patient with sclerosing peritonitis related to a prior history of peritoneal dialysis.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: RP-25

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial NECT shows extensive calcification in the left upper quadrant mesentery with tethering of adjacent bowel loops, representing an end-stage form of sclerosing mesenteritis.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: RP-26

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT shows typical surface calcification (concretion pattern) of a gallstone.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-02

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Frontal radiograph shows a feeding tube in the duodenum and a cluster of dozens of gallstones that fill the gallbladder and obstruct the GB neck .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-03

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Frontal radiograph shows a rim-calcified (eggshell) gallstone in the right upper quadrant.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-04

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: AP radiograph shows classic eggshell calcification in the right upper quadrant.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-06

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial NECT shows multiple hepatic masses, some of which have fine, amorphous calcification . This is mucinous colon carcinoma.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-08

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial NECT shows dozens of small, dense calcifications in the liver and spleen, characteristic of granulomas, probably healed histoplasmosis.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-10

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT shows peripheral rim calcification of a large hydatid cyst. Note daughter cysts (scolices) inside.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-13

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT shows marked atrophy of the pancreatic parenchyma and calcified concretions .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-16

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: AP radiograph shows a typical punctate calcified stone in the right kidney and a large staghorn calculus in the left kidney.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-20

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT shows a multicystic renal mass with calcified septa and peripheral walls . The appearance is very similar to that seen with some multilocular cystic nephromas.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-22

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT shows massively enlarged kidneys with innumerable cysts, some of which have calcified walls , due to prior hemorrhage.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-23

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT shows a calcified adrenal gland in a patient with known tuberculosis and similar lesions in the kidney and lungs.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-24

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT shows a calcified, nonfunctional left kidney , classic "putty kidney" from TB. The patient also had calcified granulomas in the lungs, adrenal gland, and nodes .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-25

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT shows a water density, nonenhancing, suprarenal mass with peripheral eggshell calcification (adrenal cyst) .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-26

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Frontal radiograph shows multiple bladder calculi with smooth, rounded shape (characterized as river stones), a common appearance.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-28

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial NECT shows a bladder calculus that has a classic jackstone, spiculated appearance , resembling the pointed surface of toy jacks.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-29

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Frontal radiograph shows a small pelvic popcorn-type calcification , one of the common forms of calcification in a degenerated uterine fibroid (leiomyoma).
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-30

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: AP radiograph shows a tooth-like calcification in the pelvis, a small part of a much larger "dermoid cyst" (mature teratoma).
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-32

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Frontal radiograph shows a cluster of calcified injection granulomas overlying the lower abdomen but located within the subcutaneous fat of the buttocks.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-36

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT shows a linear, ossified scar at the site of a prior midline abdominal incision with both cortical and medullary bone evident.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-37

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT shows extensive calcifications in the fat and ligaments of the abdominal wall and pelvis in a patient with dermatomyositis.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-40

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Frontal radiograph shows a peritoneal dialysis catheter in this diabetic patient with renal failure. There is heavy, continuous calcification of the walls of all medium- and large-sized arteries .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-44

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Frontal radiograph shows a spherical eggshell calcification in the pelvis (large common iliac artery aneurysm).
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-45

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Coronal CECT shows multiple calcified appendicoliths within a dilated appendix.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-46

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT shows an oval, fluid density mass arising from the tip of the cecum with calcification within its wall.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-48

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial NECT shows calcification of peritoneal surfaces due to "sclerosing peritonitis," a complication of chronic peritoneal dialysis. The small bowel is encased and partially obstructed.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-51

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT shows loculated fluid in the left subphrenic space with punctate and curvilinear calcifications .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-52

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT shows a large, heterogeneous adrenal mass with foci of soft tissue, necrosis, and calcification .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-53

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT shows a water density mass at the base of the mesentery with numerous thin septa, some of which are calcified .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-54

CORE_EVIDENCE_STATUS: USED
CORE_SOURCE_BASIS: Core Radiology, Second Edition — Gastrointestinal Imaging, including GI pp. 108, 117–119, 152, 162–163, and 172–173; Genitourinary material was also reviewed where relevant.
CORE_FACTS_USED:

* Chronic pancreatitis classically shows an atrophic pancreas with diffuse calcifications and a dilated/beaded duct; calcifications in the pancreatic duct distribution are described as pathognomonic.
* Calcified hepatic metastases include mucinous cancers, osteosarcoma, and treated lymphoma.
* Treated or prior fungal/granulomatous infection may leave punctate hepatic calcifications/granulomas.
* Hepatic echinococcal cysts may contain daughter cysts or floating membranes and may demonstrate peripheral calcification.
* Splenic calcification differential includes granulomatous disease, remote infarct, hematoma, calcified splenic artery aneurysm, and cystic splenic lesions.
* Cortical nephrocalcinosis is dystrophic cortical calcification associated with diffuse cortical injury.
CORE_DERIVED_CARDS:
* High-Yield: chronic pancreatitis appearance
* High-Yield: calcified hepatic metastases
* High-Yield: splenic calcification differential
* High-Yield: hepatic hydatid cyst
* Differential Drill: pancreatic calcification versus splenic artery calcification
* Master Summary synthesis
CORE_LIMITATIONS:
* Core Radiology does not present “Abdominal Calcifications” as one unified entity matching the RadPrimer/STATdx article hierarchy; relevant Core facts were retrieved across organ-specific GI/GU sections.
* Source-specific appearances not explicitly supported by Core were retained from the RadPrimer + STATdx master source rather than attributed to Core.
CORE_EVIDENCE_FILE_END
